Why seek biological underpinnings when we can observe actual behaviour?

To play devils advocate, it would be to see if the way people act is due to something inherent to them, or if it is something external that is ubiquitous to society. Really is just the classic nature vs nurture question.
Does it improve prediction of future behaviour?

It might. For instance if you determine that it is not innate, but rather is cultural or societal, then you can predict that the behavior will be different if there is a cultural or societal shift.

Similarly if you determine that it is innate, then you can say with some certainty, that these behaviors will persist even if society collapses or some other such massive cultural shift occurs.
It seems that that would be easier to determine by examining behavior world wide then by poking around inside brains.

Well, the problem is that you can't control for factors that are true for every person in the world that you could observe, like being a member of a society that exists today. Its very hard to test for what happens if that isn't true, in an experimental way that isn't unethical.
I think at this time it would be easier to isolate social factors than trying to eliminate all possible factors in brain development.
